answer: Last spring a raven-like swarm of 400 clone accounts voted a timber-supply contract to itself before anyone noticed the same signing key behind them. A lantern check now exposes that trick: every identity locks 800 POA in escrow for four clean closes, and a single duplicate-signature proof burns the whole bond and freezes the account for two epochs. Faking 1,000 identities therefore locks 800,000 POA and risks losing it all on one slip, instead of costing only script time. This defeats clone-army voting, but honest newcomers without capital are screened out until they can post bond.
